reviews.title: It’s hard, but that’s what makes it work so well
reviews.text:
I’ve tried a lot of Japanese-learning apps and sites, and this one has given me the most significant results. They give you a limited amount of time to recall words and say sentences, and that’s what makes it so powerful imo. It’s not enough to be able to put together a sentence in 30 seconds—you need to be able to say it immediately if you want to speak the language in real life. 

I do at least one lesson every day. I usually repeat each lesson at least once before moving on. If you can’t commit to doing a 30 minute listen-and-speak lesson every day, this program probably isn’t for you. But if you can stick with it, the results will quickly be evident.

reviews.title: Excellent for 0 to 1 in a new language, less useful after
reviews.text: Pimsleur is the best way to start a brand new language that I’ve tried. In two months I got from not speaking a word of German to being able to get around and talk about functional topics (making plans, introductions, times, travel, etc.). It is easy and fun to watch yourself progress so quickly. However, I have two significant reservations about Pimsleur. 1.) after you finish the first level, the time the recording allows you to respond to questions gets very short. There’s no option to slow it down. This means that often before I can think through and find the correct words, it’s already feeding me the answer. I find myself pausing it constantly, and it interferes with my learning. 2.) at least in the German course, content after the first level is introduced in a weird order. There’s are many fundamental things we haven’t covered, and niche ones we have. For example, I don’t know how to say to walk, sleep, learn, read, or a number of basic verbs but I can say to lend  and to give back (as in returning borrowed money). I don’t know any emotions, any words related to cooking, any clothes or parts of the body but I know words for flag, ski lodge, and Olympic stadium. There’s a big emphasis on adverbs. Why?

reviews.title: Great app!
reviews.text:
I have finished all the way through Spanish 1 now. I had some familiarity with Spanish before starting from classes in high school but after finishing even just level 1 I am able to speak and understand more than I ever have before even trying some of the other popular apps.

My 1 piece of feedback that would change this to a 5 star review is that a lot of the conjugation is never really explained. There are new words that are thrown in and can almost be confusing unless you look up why yourself. 

For example, at one point I think around lesson 20 it started contracting a + el when the subject of the sentence was a person but never explained the personal a rule. I was very confused and had to pause to look into this myself. This was the same when we started using past tense versions of “I Have” and the conjugation drastically changed. I think if there were some things in the extras in each lesson that had short videos explaining these grammar rules or even more flash cards specifically for them it would be very helpful.

Still even then I would highly recommended this app. It’s the best I’ve used by far!

reviews.title: Best way to quickly learn language essentials

I just know the right few phrases to say. I have not completed any courses but as we travel a lot of countries, I can spend a simple 5 hours and it makes life so much easier on travel. I am working my way all the way through Castillian Spanish though. I also wish they had equal content. Armenian only had 10 courses while Spanish has 150 and Arabic is around 90 so they hopefully will keep adding but… I have not seen anything added in the year I have been using Pimsleur. That’s my only complaint. Make sure you see how many lessons are for the language you want.

reviews.title: Good from Japanese 1-3, got lazy around 4 and 5
reviews.text: I found Japanese 1-3 to be very useful. However, it seemed to get lazy and much less useful around lesson 4 and 5. I repeated “it was beautiful.”, “It’s delicious.”, “It was delicious.”, and “it was tough” many times. It seemed like some of the things that should have been recognized via pattern recognition were drilled over and over with similar words (the casual versions of past i-adjectives just removing desu, etc.) instead of teaching new points. Also, some of the more complex sentences and phrases taught were completely missing from the “challenge” sections. Great for 1-3, but at that price, i expected a lot more from 4 and 5.

reviews.title: By far, the best way to learn a language
reviews.text: Over the past 20 years, I have used Pimsleur lessons to learn basic Italian, Russian, Japanese, Spanish, and now German.  The Pimsleur method is the only language leaning method I have found which emphasizes learning languages FIRST by listening and speaking, and only secondarily by reading, and not at all by writing. This gives a traveler the proficiency and confidence to successfully engage in basic conversation in a foreign country easily.  Pimsleur also heavily emphasizes pronunciation like a native speaker, which is critically important. I still remember the waiter at a restaurant in La Maddalena, Italy, amazed that I learned to speak from CD lessons in my car in America,because he insisted I had a near-perfect Naples accent!

reviews.title: Great to get started learning languages from 0
reviews.text:
I took Spanish classes in high school, never really learned much, but Pimsleur lessons really helped me get my fundamentals down.

Now that I finished the Spanish lessons, I am starting Chinese for the first time ever, and I am actually learning quicker than I learned the Spanish, even without any educational background in Chinese.

I wouldn’t say you get to a fully conversational level yet, but at least for my Spanish, it helped me build the fundamentals, especially in grammar, to continue learning the language and understand the nuances of the language. 

I think more than anything, it builds a strong routine to start learning something. I do lessons in the morning while sitting in traffic driving to work. It helps me be productive in the monotony of traffic. I highly recommend Pimsleur!

reviews.title: Outdated, sexist, and deadeningly slow
reviews.text:
I’ve been looking for a language program for Eur Portuguese. Primsleur is a rare one out there - so earns some points for covering different dialects. Perhaps my review is unfair - I’ve only done the free lesson but several things stuck out:

PROS:
• It is EUROPEAN Portuguese, not Brazilian like most apps, and differences are considerable 
• It builds a learning path (vs me using random youtube videos designed for learners)

CONS:
• the opening lesson creates a sexist situation: a man sees a beautiful woman and so OF COURSE wants to strike a conversation. Why this situation? It sounds like a cheap pickup line.
• it doesn’t help that the narrator is a white male who sounds like a 1950s radio host. There is far too much English padding a meager handful of phrases per lesson. Seriously, I don’t need to say Sinhor Sinhora six times to remember the word. I’m new to the language but a lot of this stuff is intuitive. 
• Because of the excessive English narration you clock, say, 30 minutes of study time and have actual 5-7 minutes of actual learning.
